summary: This Docusaurus plugin creates plain-Markdown mirrors of blog posts alongside their HTML pages, plus two kinds of text indexes: a site-wide `/llms.txt` file listing all articles by category, and per-series `/llms/<series>.txt` bundles concatenating related articles. It reads all published blog posts, converts their MDX to Markdown, writes the mirrors and indexes during the build process, and gracefully handles conversion failures without breaking the entire build.

explanations.32: withFileTypes: true tells the function to return file/directory metadata objects instead of just names, so we can check whether each entry is a directory or file.
explanations.35: The three dots (...) spread the results from the recursive call into the found array, flattening nested directory results into a single list.
explanations.49: This regex adds a hyphen between a lowercase letter (or digit) followed by an uppercase letter — so 'myTitle' becomes 'my-Title' before lowercasing.
explanations.51: normalize('NFD') breaks accented characters into their base letter plus separate accent marks, preparing them to be stripped out on the next line.
explanations.62: If the post's frontmatter already has a 'slug' field, use it; otherwise fall back to deriving the slug from the directory structure.
explanations.76: front-matter library parses the YAML header and separates it from the content; we extract just the attributes (the YAML metadata).
explanations.82: path.relative() gets the directory path relative to the blog root, then split and rejoin replaces platform-specific separators (backslash on Windows) with forward slashes.
explanations.108: The ternary checks if date is a Date object; if so, toISOString() gives a full timestamp string, and slice(0, 10) extracts just the 'YYYY-MM-DD' portion.
explanations.146: new Map() creates a dictionary where keys are tag names and values are arrays of posts with that tag.
explanations.179: Spreading byTag.keys() into an array and sorting ensures we iterate through categories in alphabetical order for the final output.
explanations.207: Destructuring [seriesName, seriesPosts] unpacks each key-value pair from the Map as we iterate.
explanations.236: new Set() from routesPaths creates a fast lookup table so checking if a post's permalink was actually published is O(1) instead of O(n).
explanations.256: We prepend the metadata comment and title/description header to the converted Markdown content.
explanations.269: post.permalink.replace(//$/, '') removes a trailing slash if present, so '/blog/foo/' becomes '/blog/foo' to form the filename '/blog/foo.md'.
explanations.273: Only non-draft, non-unlisted posts are added to the index — this prevents hidden articles from appearing in the llms.txt catalog.
